- [neg-a-disjunctive-slice-family-is-still-a-finite-family-if-a] A disjunctive slice family is still a finite family. If a construction needs 'variable u small OR variable v small', that is the union of two finite unions of slices and costs only a constant factor in the form count -- so 'which variable is small varies with the input' does not defeat finiteness. Check the disjunction before recording that a slice construction failed.
  Trigger: A diagnostic reports that no single variable can be bounded, and the run is about to conclude that no finite family of specialisations exists.
- [neg-before-funding-a-descent-or-minimal-counterexample-route] Before funding a descent or minimal-counterexample route, check what the minimality hypothesis is actually worth: if the property being descended on is already a theorem for a density-one set, minimality contributes nothing there and the whole usable content of the induction is confined to the thin set, which is usually the original difficulty re-imported.
  Trigger: A route proposes infinite descent or minimal counterexample on a set whose complement is already characterized by a proved lemma covering almost all integers.
- [neg-before-recording-a-lemma-as-blocked-on-an-undeposited] Before recording a lemma as blocked on an undeposited classical source, ask whether the needed instance can be derived at a fixed small modulus — a derivation often costs one Generator round, keeps the run's zero-undeposited-dependency record intact, and yields effective constants that the citation route does not provide.
  Trigger: A source hunt for a standard analytic input (Mertens for progressions, a character sum bound, a divisor asymptotic) returns either nothing or only statements with non-effective implied constants, and a lemma is about to be marked blocked.

  Trigger: A source or verifier packet reports reading a primary source 'directly' or 'verbatim from the retrieved primary text', and `references/source/` or `references/.extracted/` contains no corresponding artifact for it.

Before a quoted relation set becomes load-bearing, run a constant-cost internal-consistency check on the quotation itself --- count DISTINCT arguments against the declared group order, test whether any member appears on two sides with opposite signs, and check the quoted display against the source's own neighbouring lemmas --- and record 'quoted accurately' and 'usable as printed' as two separate verdicts.

- [neg-do-not-spend-repeated-bounded-search-budget-hunting-a] Do not spend repeated bounded-search budget hunting a published external proof of a target that is an item of a freshly posted proofs-withheld challenge document before the challenge's own disclosure or outcome-report date; scope the literature pass to pre-challenge independent mathematics once, record the challenge's per-item proof-status classification with provenance, and schedule a dated re-check instead of re-searching.

- [neg-do-not-treat-a-hardness-proxy-internal-to-your-own] Do not treat a hardness proxy internal to your own certificate family — the minimal parameter value your forms need to reach a target — as an instance of a source's named exceptional class (its 'wild', 'exceptional', 'sporadic' set). Read the source's definition first: the two usually measure different things, and the coincidence that both mean 'hard' is not a shared definition.

- [neg-do-not-treat-a-single-spelling-arxiv-api-sweep-on-a] Do not treat a name-based arXiv sweep as complete until you have queried every circulating spelling of the diacritic (ASCII o, double-acute o, umlaut o for a Hungarian surname) plus at least one orthogonal subject query: the API matches the indexed glyph literally, and the paper defining a run's central vocabulary can sit in the one spelling nobody tried.
  Trigger: A literature search for a problem named after an author whose surname carries a diacritic (Erdos, Godel, Renyi, Turan, Poincare, Mobius) is about to be recorded as exhaustive on the strength of name queries.
- [neg-for-a-value-set-of-a-bilinear-form-c-au-bv-muv-with-m-1] For a value set of a bilinear form c + au + bv + muv with m >= 1, every value below N has min(u,v) <= sqrt(N/m). So the value set below N is a union of O(sqrt N) arithmetic progressions rather than O(N) points, and it can be marked by strided in-place writes with no division. Reach for this before accepting a compute budget as the binding constraint on a coverage sweep.
  Trigger: A run is sieving the value sets of bilinear or multilinear forms up to a bound, the runtime is superlinear in the bound, and a decade of range is about to be declared unaffordable.
- [neg-in-any-argument-that-factors-a-quantity-as-d-e-and-reads] In any argument that factors a quantity as d*e and reads the two factors back into a form's arguments, treat the bound on each factor as a separate obligation: 'likewise', 'by symmetry', or 'similarly' applied to the cofactor is a defect flag even when the form is symmetric in its variables, because the domain restriction usually sits on only one argument.
  Trigger: A proof or a statement's strategy section establishes a lower bound on one factor of a factorization and extends it to the cofactor by an appeal to symmetry, while at least one of the value sets involved is indexed over strictly positive rather than nonnegative arguments.
- [neg-keep-effective-and-ineffective-finiteness-rigidly-apart-and] Keep effective and ineffective finiteness rigidly apart, and derive the consequence of the ineffective form explicitly rather than by analogy: an ineffective finiteness statement about a set of primes leaves unresolved the entire multiplicative semigroup those primes generate, which is infinite, so it does not reduce to 'all but finitely many integers'.
  Trigger: A run observes that an exceptional set of primes appears finite and reasons about what proving finiteness would buy, or evaluates an external claim that such a conjecture is 'at least as hard' as the parent problem.
- [neg-splitting-parameters-into-finer-residue-classes-never] Splitting parameters into finer residue classes never reduces the arity of a parameterized family. Arity drops only when a parameter becomes determined by the others, not when it is restricted to a progression -- a parameter confined to an arithmetic progression is still a free parameter, merely reindexed.
  Trigger: A route proposes to eliminate a variable from a family of forms by refining the moduli, splitting into more forms with larger modulus, or 'more specific residue class comparisons'.
- [neg-to-classify-all-polynomial-dictionaries-between-a] To classify all polynomial dictionaries between a multilinear form and a product normal form, do not fit an ansatz -- use degree additivity. If the target is degree at most 1 in each variable and the normal form contains a single product term, then for each variable the degrees of the factors sum to 1, so every variable is owned by exactly one factor, the ownership maps are finitely many, and each can be solved exactly and accepted only on exact symbolic cancellation.
  Trigger: A run needs the correspondence between printed polynomial forms and an arithmetic relation, and is considering fitting coefficients on a sample grid.
- [neg-treat-an-external-cross-verification-call-that-fails-at-the] Treat an external cross-verification call that fails at the transport or billing layer as a tool failure with no score, never as a returned score of zero: it must not force a non-PASS verdict, and it must be recorded so the verdict is known to rest on the referee's own derivation with no independent corroboration.
  Trigger: A Verifier's mandated external cross-verification returns an HTTP error envelope (402 credit exhaustion, 429, timeout) instead of a rubric result, and the verdict rules key off a numeric score.
- [neg-when-a-bounded-source-search-for-a-run-s-single-missing] When a bounded source search for a run's single missing datum discovers that the target's own source document attests the result is proven but embargoed with a dated disclosure, classify the empty search as a dated bounded negative and convert the run to a documented restart-obligation stop with the verified reduction banked and dated re-check triggers scheduled; do not reclassify the target as obstruction-risk, do not open a local research program to race the embargo, and do not treat the attestation itself as a mathematical source for its own conclusion.
  Trigger: A Searcher trace closes NO_QUALIFYING_SOURCE for a named-datum request, and among its findings is that the problem statement's own source (challenge/benchmark/announcement) classifies the target as proven-with-withheld-proof and names a concrete future disclosure or outcome-report date.
- [neg-when-a-covering-or-representation-target-is-verified-to] When a covering or representation target is verified to IMPLY a famous open problem, that verified reduction is the run's bankable result and the covering direction should be scoped out immediately — but the run must not stop there, because the partial and structural results in the target's direction are usually still unproved and still reachable.
  Trigger: A run establishes, with a fresh Verifier PASS, that proving its printed target would prove a named long-standing open conjecture, and a terminal stop is being considered on the grounds that no route can succeed.
- [neg-when-a-per-object-search-has-a-hopeless-bound-exhaust-a] When a per-object search has a hopeless bound (exhaust a parameter up to something linear in the object), invert the loop order: fix the parameters and let the object be generated, so that the objects produced form arithmetic progressions covered by a sieve. This converts a bounded negative ('no solution with parameter <= D') into an exhaustive certification, at no extra cost.
  Trigger: A census or classification requires, per object, exhausting a parameter whose naive bound grows with the object, and the run is about to declare its result conditional on a search cutoff.
- [neg-when-a-printed-target-is-a-repaired-version-of-a-system-an] When a printed target is a repaired version of a system an earlier run refuted, re-establish transcription, coverage data, and the source package from the primary document rather than inheriting them, but do read the earlier run first — it usually identifies exactly which element was added and why, which is the fastest route to the new system's structure.

- [neg-when-a-project-s-whole-toolkit-sits-on-one-side-of-a-source] When a project's whole toolkit sits on one side of a source's own dichotomy, build the other side before attacking anything harder: the missing half is usually derivable from the same source by moving one symbol, costs one bounded search, and its hard instances are the cheapest available test of whether the two halves are independent or redundant.
  Trigger: A run notices that every construction it holds instantiates one branch of a classification the literature states symmetrically (Type I/Type II, Case A/Case B, split/inert), and the other branch is undeveloped in the workspace though not in the literature.
- [neg-when-a-run-inherits-a-finite-table-of-certificates-from-a] When a run inherits a finite table of certificates from a source document, test whether the table's apparent parameter ceiling is a theorem or a tabulation artifact: reconstruct the defining identity and search it directly, because a bound that was only ever read off the given rows will often dissolve into an infinite family at the same degree.
  Trigger: A verified result is stated over a finite list of forms taken from a problem statement, and some derived parameter is observed to be bounded across all rows without any proof that it must be.
- [neg-when-a-source-proves-that-every-viable-method-must-fail-on] When a source proves that every viable method must fail on a distinguished thin subfamily, run that failure as a cheap filter on any new construction before formalizing it: a construction that succeeds where the theorem says nothing can is evidence of your own error, and the filter costs seconds while a spurious result on a famous problem costs the run its credibility.
  Trigger: A run produces a new explicit family or construction aimed at a problem whose literature contains a vanishing/impossibility statement on a distinguished subclass (odd perfect squares, a square congruence class, a degenerate fibre).
